text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are concerned about your infant's bilious vomiting and abdominal distension. How old is the baby, and at what age did they first pass meconium?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal barium enema rules out Hirschsprung disease, so I suspect a functional obstruction. I will order a sweat chloride test to check for cystic fibrosis, which is a common cause of meconium ileus. REQUEST TEST: Sweat_Chloride_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: With Hirschsprung disease and cystic fibrosis ruled out, I suspect an anatomical defect such as meconium plug syndrome or small left colon syndrome, especially given the home birth context. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the bilious vomiting and distal obstruction on X-ray, but normal barium enema and sweat test, I suspect a small bowel obstruction like ileal atresia. Have you noticed any specific bowel sounds, and was the mother diabetic or did she take any teratogenic medications during pregnancy? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ultrasound and barium enema effectively rule out meconium plug syndrome and Hirschsprung disease. Since the infant has a distal obstruction but no evidence of cystic fibrosis or colonic anomalies, I suspect an anatomical blockage higher up. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jejunal Atresia
